data.name: Eliphaz
data.gender_notes: Eliphaz is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew language, Eliphaz means 'my God is abundance'. This name is significant in the Old Testament, where Eliphaz is a wise and elderly friend of Job. In the book of Job, Eliphaz offers comforting counsel to Job during his time of suffering. This name symbolizes faith, wisdom, and divine protection. The name Eliphaz carries the meaning “My God is abundance” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Eliphaz usually hope their child will grow to embody my god is abundance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing God's abundant love and wisdom.
data.etymology: Eliphaz belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My God is abundance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eliphaz total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: אֱלִיפַז
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אֱלִיפַז (אֱלִ-פַז) - חָכָם, נוֹצֵר, וּמֶלֶךְ צָדִיק. בְּתוֹרָתוֹ, הִיא תְפִלָה, וְלֵב שָׂמֵחַ. הִיא גֶזֶר, שֶׁמְזַמְּנוּ לְהַגְדִיר אֶת תְפִלָה וְלֵב. אֱלִיפַז, שֵם מְעֻבָּד, שֶׁבוֹאוֹ, אֵלָיו, יִשְׂגַּע. הִיא חֶפְצוֹ, שֶׁל כֹּל, אֲשֶׁר, יְבָרֵךְ.

in_greek.name: Ἐλιφάζ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Ἐλιφάζ (Ἐλιφάζ) ἦταν σοφός, φρόνιμος και ἀπάνθρωπος. Ἀρχαῖος Εἰρηναῖος ὁ Ἀλεξανδρεῖος ἔγραψε, ὅτι Ἐλιφάζ ἦταν ἕνας τῶν τρεῖς ἀνδρῶν, οἱ ὅποι ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός, νὰ εἰσέλθουν στὸ πλήρωμα της εὐσεβείας. Ἐλιφάζ, ὁ σοφός, ἦταν μὲ τὴν ἀπάνθρωπη φύση, ἀπὸ τὴν ἀρχαιότητα.

in_latin.name: Eliphaz
in_latin.long_meaning: Eliphaz, nomen sapientis, sacerdotis, et regis sapientis. In antiqua ecclesia, Eliphaz significabat prudentiam, sacerdotalem dignitatem, et regalem sapientiam. Eliphaz, nomen sanctum, est in libris sacris, ubi describitur sapientia et perfectio moralis.

in_english.name: Eliphaz
in_english.meaning: prudent, wise, king of the wise ones
in_english.long_meaning: Eliphaz is a name of wisdom, a name that signifies prudence, priestly dignity, and royal wisdom. In ancient times, Eliphaz was used to describe a wise and just leader. As a name, Eliphaz is rich in biblical and historical significance, evoking images of wisdom, leadership, and spiritual guidance. In modern times, Eliphaz is used as a given name for boys, symbolizing a strong sense of purpose and a desire for wisdom and knowledge.

data.cultural_impact: Eliphaz is a name found in the Old Testament of the Bible, signifying the rich and wise heritage of Hebrew tradition. It is a name that holds significant meaning in the Jewish community and beyond, reflecting a deep connection to the Judeo-Christian religious tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Eliphaz conveys the profound idea that God is our source of abundance. In times of hardship and sorrow, this name serves as a reminder of the comforting presence of God. Eliphaz, as a name, symbolizes wisdom, faith, and the divine protection that comes from trusting in a higher power. Eliphaz is a name that inspires reverence, humility, and the hope that, even in the face of adversity, God is sufficient and holds the abundance that sustains us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eliphaz, meaning "my God is abundance," reflects the deep faith and trust in the divine providence of the bearer. It speaks of a life lived in gratitude for God's endless gifts and blessings.

biblical_reference.note: Eliphaz was one of Job's comforters in the book of Job.

historical_references.reference:
Eliphaz the Temanite is mentioned in Job 2:11, 42:11 as one of the three friends who came to comfort Job in his suffering. According to the text, Eliphaz is a wise man from Teman, a region in Edom.
Time period: Pre-exilic period, around 6th century BCE
Context: Book of Job

Eliphaz, a son of Esau mentioned in Genesis 36:4-5, is an ancestor of the Edomite kings. He is also the father of Teman, the region from which Eliphaz the Temanite in the Book of Job hails.
Time period: Early 2nd millennium BCE
Context: Book of Genesis
